bullets.title: DELL blows out estimates; AI server cycle accelerating well beyond Street
bullets.body: DELL reported Q2 revenue of $47B (+58% YoY), crushing guidance of $44-45B, with AI server revenue of $16.4B (+100% YoY) and a $95B backlog across 6,500+ customers. FY27 guidance raised to $192B revenue (+70%) and $25.50 EPS (+150%), with AI server revenue now guided to $74B (3x YoY). Demand exceeds supply — constraints in DRAM, NAND, CPUs, optics remain the binding limiter, not demand; DELL OpEx at 8% of revenue is lowest in its 42-year history.

bullets.title: AVGO: ~$5B trimmed from F2027 AI revenue est on TPU timing; GCP ramp still strong
bullets.body: UBS trimmed ~$5B from Broadcom's F2027 AI revenue estimate (now ~$130B) citing aggressive TPU unit shipment assumptions, though Anthropic TPU shipments are still estimated at $2.5B in FQ3 ramping to $3.3B in FQ4. GCP-related AI revenues expected to step up ~$2B Q/Q in FQ3 and another ~$1.5B in FQ4; OpenAI contributes ~$1.25B/$12B in C2026/C2027. PT cut $485→$470, Buy maintained.

bullets.title: NVDA in advanced talks to acquire Hugging Face for ~$12.9B + $1B retention
bullets.body: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire Hugging Face at a ~$12.9B valuation plus a $1B retention package for staff, with a deal potentially closing this week. Microsoft had also held talks but those have ended. Hugging Face had previously rejected an NVDA $500M investment offer at a $7B valuation in January 2025.

bullets.title: AI data center capex on parabolic path; TSMC tool needs almost doubled YoY
bullets.body: TSMC's quarterly chipmaking tool requirements nearly doubled year-over-year, reflecting the scale of AI infrastructure buildout. PwC projects AI data center spending will reach ~$32 trillion by 2050. HPE server ASPs are up 50-100% with no meaningful demand destruction, and memory spot prices remain firm despite some DDR5/DDR4 softness.

bullets.title: Enterprise AI security: $33B agentic identity market emerging as next spending wave
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley identifies a $33B market opportunity in agentic identity security as AI agents gain access to sensitive enterprise systems. CRWD's Falcon'26 event is anchoring its 'Autonomously Securing AI' strategy around SafeMind, a purpose-built security model for agentic defense, with management telegraphing potential FY31E ARR targets of $10B (implying 11-13% CAGR from FY27 vs. current 26% guidance).

bullets.title: PANW: Strong F4Q26 beat across all metrics; platformization gaining clear traction
bullets.body: PANW posted F4Q26 revenue +34% YoY (1.7% above consensus), NGS ARR +63% YoY with $970M NNARR ($170M above guidance), and record 220 net new platformizations (+44% YoY) driven by Mythos. FY27 NGS ARR guidance of $11.125B (+22%) beat consensus by ~$185M; stock is up 97% YTD vs IGV +1% and trades at 52x EV/CY27E FCF.

bullets.title: Trucking rates up 30% YTD, structural pressure on consumer margins through 2027
bullets.body: Truck rates are up ~30% YoY driven by supply tightening (not demand), with spot rates elevated since Nov 2025 and contract rates (~75% of freight) only now beginning to catch up. Trump administration policies and a Supreme Court ruling on freight broker liability further constrain driver supply; Citi sees rates continuing to rise into 2027+ absent a housing recovery, adding a structural 10-15% to an already 10-15% equilibrium adjustment.

bullets.title: JPM derivatives: NDX upside, memory-to-semis rotation, healthcare at inflection
bullets.body: JPMorgan's August equity derivatives monthly highlights NDX upside and mean-reversion trade ideas, a memory-to-semis rotation visible in Delta-One flows, and healthcare as a potential inflection point following Q2 earnings volatility. Dispersion trading opportunities are also cited on equity volatility.

bullets.title: Roth Capital tracking enterprise AI budget allocation and hyperscaler platform preference
bullets.body: Roth Capital is fielding a survey targeting senior IT decision-makers at large and mid-sized U.S. enterprises to map AI spend intent and platform preference across AWS, GCP, and Azure. Key metrics include AI ROI, business areas benefiting most (customer service, data analytics, supply chain), and adoption barriers across ML, NLP, RPA, computer vision, and predictive analytics.

bullets.title: Hong Kong/Asia equities: Hang Seng +1.2%, Tech +2.0%; gold-linked names weaker
bullets.body: The Hang Seng rose 1.20% to 25,025 and the Hang Seng Tech Index gained 1.98% to 4,461 in mid-morning trading on Sep 2. Non-ferrous metal names declined on gold weakness, while broader tech outperformed. Asian 52-week low breadth remains heavy — 76 names at lows vs. 24 at highs, with Technology Services sector showing 1 high vs. 10 lows.

bullets.title: LatAm macro deteriorating: Chile GDP slashed to 0.4%, Peru inflation at 4.44%, Colombia borrowing surges
bullets.body: Chile's Imacec fell 1.5% YoY in July (worst since March 2023) on mining contraction of -9.3%, driving full-year GDP growth forecasts as low as 0.4%. Peru's Lima CPI accelerated to 4.44% YoY in August — third consecutive rise and highest since September 2023, well above the BCR's 1-3% target. Colombia is seeking $11.1B in additional 2027 borrowing capacity tied to a 1.3pp-of-GDP deterioration in its primary balance.

bullets.title: SPGI Capital IQ Pro spinout: JPM skeptical, math doesn't work at reported $7-9B valuation
bullets.body: S&P Global is exploring a spinout of Capital IQ Pro (estimated ~$930M revenue, low-single-digit growth), but JPMorgan argues the $7-9B Bloomberg valuation implies multiples far above comps like FactSet (5x LTM EV/revenue). Separating Capital IQ from SNL and Visible Alpha would be dis-synergistic; JPM argues the cleaner re-rating path is organic MI execution, not a spinout. SPGI stock gained ~1% on the news while S&P 500 fell 0.7%.
